en: Abu al-Tahir, Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Sarh, mawla of Banu Umayyah, narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed me: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) undertook the Battle of Tabuk intending [to confront] the Byzantines and the Christian Arabs in the Levant (al-Sham). Ibn Shihab said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me that 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b—who was Ka'b's guide from among his sons when he went blind—said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik narrating his account when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in the Battle of Tabuk. Ka'b ibn Malik said: I never stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in any expedition that he undertook except in the Battle of Tabuk, although I had stayed behind in the Battle of Badr, and he did not reproach anyone who stayed behind from it; rather, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and the Muslims had only set out intending [to intercept] the caravan of Quraysh until Allah brought them and their enemy together without an appointment. And indeed, I was present with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) on the Night of al-'Aqabah when we pledged our allegiance to Islam, and I would not prefer to have been at Badr instead of it, even though Badr is more mentioned among people than it. And the account of my staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in the Battle of Tabuk was that I was never stronger nor more affluent than I was when I stayed behind from him in that expedition. By Allah, I had never before gathered two mounts until I gathered both of them in that expedition. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) set out for it in intense heat, facing a long journey and deserts, and facing a numerous enemy. So he made their affair clear to the Muslims so that they might prepare for their expedition, and he informed them of the direction he intended. And the Muslims with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) were many, and no preserving record compiled them—meaning thereby the register (diwan). Ka'b said: Rarely would a man intend to absent himself thinking that that would remain hidden as long as no revelation came down concerning it from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) set out for that expedition when the fruits were ripe and the shade was pleasant, and I was inclined toward them. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and the Muslims with him made their preparations, and I began going out in the morning to prepare with them, but I would return without having accomplished anything, saying to myself: 'I am capable of doing that whenever I wish.' That continued to linger with me until the people were earnest in their departure, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) set out in the morning with the Muslims, while I had not accomplished anything of my preparation. Then I went out in the morning and returned without having accomplished anything. That continued to linger with me until they hastened and the campaign had advanced far. Then I intended to set out and catch up with them—and would that I had done so! But it was not destined for me. So whenever I went out among the people after the departure of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), it grieved me that I saw no one as an example for me except a man suspected of hypocrisy or a man whom Allah had excused among the weak. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. Then he said while sitting among the people at Tabuk: 'What has Ka'b ibn Malik done?' A man from Banu Salimah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, his two garments and looking at his two flanks have detained him.' Mu'adh ibn Jabal said to him: 'What an evil thing you have said! By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we have known nothing about him but good.' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained silent. While he was in that state, he saw a man clad in white emerging through the mirage. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Be Abu Khaythamah!' And lo, it was Abu Khaythamah al-Ansari, and he was the one who had given a sa' of dates in charity when the hypocrites mocked him. Ka'b ibn Malik said: When the news reached me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was heading back from Tabuk, my distress overtook me, and I began devising falsehood, saying: 'How can I escape his displeasure tomorrow?' and seeking the assistance of every wise person among my family in that matter. But when it was said to me that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had arrived nearby, falsehood vanished from me until I knew that I would never be saved from him by anything, so I resolved to speak the truth to him. And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) arrived in the morning. Whenever he returned from a journey, he would start by visiting the mosque, pray two rak'ahs in it, and then sit for the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began making excuses to him and swearing to him, and they were eighty-odd men. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) accepted from them what was apparent, took their pledge of allegiance, asked Allah to forgive them, and entrusted their inner secrets to Allah, until I came. When I greeted him with peace, he smiled with the smile of someone angry, then said: 'Come forward.' So I came walking until I sat before him. He said to me: 'What held you back? Had you not bought your riding animal?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else among the people of this world, I would consider that I could escape his displeasure with an excuse, for I have been gifted with argumentative skill. But, by Allah, I know that if I were to tell you today a false statement with which you would be pleased with me, Allah would soon make you displeased with me; and if I tell you a true statement about which you find fault with me, I hope for Allah’s pardon in it. By Allah, I had no excuse. By Allah, I was never stronger nor more affluent than I was when I stayed behind from you.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'As for this man, he has spoken the truth. So stand up until Allah decrees regarding you.' So I stood up, and men from Banu Salimah stirred and followed me, saying to me: 'By Allah, we have never known you to commit a sin before this. You failed to offer an excuse to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) such as those who stayed behind offered him, for the Messenger of Allah’s (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) asking forgiveness for you would have been sufficient for your sin.' He said: By Allah, they continued reproaching me until I intended to return to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and contradict myself. He said: Then I said to them: 'Did anyone meet this with me?' They said: 'Yes, two men met it with you; they said the like of what you said, and it was said to them the like of what was said to you.' He said: I asked: 'Who are they?' They said: 'Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-'Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi.' He said: They mentioned to me two righteous men who had been present at Badr, in whom there was an example. He said: So I proceeded when they mentioned them to me. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade the Muslims from speaking to us three from among those who stayed behind from him. He said: So the people avoided us. And he said: They changed toward us until the earth appeared strange to me in my soul, and it was not the earth that I knew. We remained like that for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they surrendered and sat in their houses weeping. But as for me, I was the youngest of the people and the hardiest of them, so I would go out, attend the prayer, and walk in the marketplaces, and no one would speak to me. And I would come to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and greet him with peace while he was in his gathering after the prayer, saying to myself: 'Did he move his lips to return the greeting of peace or not?' Then I would pray near him and glance covertly at him; whenever I turned to my prayer, he would look at me, and whenever I turned toward him, he would look away from me. Until when that harshness from the Muslims became prolonged for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of the orchard of Abu Qatadah—and he was my cousin and the dearest of people to me—and I greeted him with peace, but by Allah, he did not return the greeting of peace to me. I said to him: 'O Abu Qatadah, I adjure you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?' He said: He remained silent. So I returned and adjured him, but he remained silent. So I returned and adjured him, and he said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' My eyes overflowed with tears, and I turned away until I climbed back over the wall. While I was walking in the market of Medina, suddenly a Nabataean among the Nabataeans of the people of the Levant (al-Sham)—from among those who had come with food grain to sell in Medina—was saying: 'Who will direct me to Ka'b ibn Malik?' He said: People began pointing him toward me until he came to me and handed me a letter from the King of Ghassan. And I was a literate man, so I read it, and in it was: 'To proceed: Indeed, it has reached us that your companion has treated you harshly, and Allah has not placed you in an abode of humiliation or neglect, so join us and we will console you.' He said: I said when I read it: 'And this also is part of the trial.' So I turned with it toward the baking oven and burned it therein. Until when forty nights of the fifty had passed and revelation was delayed, suddenly a messenger of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to me and said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commands you to stay away from your wife.' He said: I asked: 'Shall I divorce her, or what should I do?' He said: 'No, rather stay away from her and do not approach her.' He said: And he sent the like of that to my two companions. He said: So I said to my wife: 'Join your family and remain with them until Allah decrees concerning this matter.' He said: Then the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed Hilal ibn Umayyah is a ruined old man with no servant; would you dislike that I serve him?' He said: 'No, but he must not approach you.' She said: 'By Allah, he has no movement toward anything, and by Allah, he has not ceased weeping since what occurred of his matter began until this day of his.' He said: Some of my family said to me: 'If only you would ask permission of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) regarding your wife, for he has permitted the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah to serve him.' He said: I said: 'I will not ask permission of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) regarding her, for what do I know what the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would say if I asked his permission regarding her while I am a young man?' He said: So I remained like that for ten nights, thereby completing fifty nights for us since speaking to us had been forbidden. He said: Then I prayed the Fajr prayer on the morning of fifty nights on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the condition that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned of us—my soul had become constricted for me and the earth had become constricted for me despite its vastness—I heard the voice of a caller who had climbed atop Sal' saying at the top of his voice: 'O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice with glad tidings!' He said: I fell down in prostration, and I knew that relief had arrived. He said: And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) announced to the people Allah's acceptance of repentance for us when he prayed the Fajr prayer, so the people went out giving us glad tidings. Bringers of glad tidings went toward my two companions, and a man galloped on a horse toward me, while a runner from Aslam sprinted toward me and climbed the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I had heard giving me glad tidings came to me, I stripped off my two garments for him and clothed him with them for his glad tidings; by Allah, I possessed no other garments than them on that day. And I borrowed two garments and wore them, and I set out heading toward the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), with people meeting me troop after troop congratulating me on the repentance, saying: 'May Allah's acceptance of repentance over you bring you joy!' Until I entered the mosque, and there was the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sitting in the mosque with people around him. Then Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah stood up running until he shook hands with me and congratulated me; by Allah, no man from among the Emigrants (Muhajirun) stood up except him. He said: And Ka'b would never forget that for Talhah. Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) with peace, he said while his face was beaming with joy: 'Rejoice with glad tidings of the best day that has passed over you since your mother gave birth to you!' He said: I asked: 'Is it from you, O Messenger of Allah, or from Allah?' He replied: 'No, rather it is from Allah.' And whenever the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was joyful, his face would illuminate as if his face were a piece of the moon; he said: and we used to recognize that. He said: When I sat before him, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I divest myself of my wealth as charity to Allah and to His Messenger (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Retain some of your wealth, for that is better for you.' He said: I said: 'Then I retain my portion that is in Khaybar.' He said: And I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah only saved me through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I shall not speak except truth as long as I live.' He said: By Allah, I do not know that anyone among the Muslims has been tested by Allah in truthfulness of speech, from when I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) down to this day of mine, better than what Allah has tested me with. By Allah, I have never deliberately told a lie from when I said that to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) down to this day of mine, and I hope that Allah will preserve me in what remains. He said: Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Allah has already forgiven the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of difficulty after the hearts of a party of them had almost inclined [to doubt], and then He forgave them. Indeed, He was to them Kind and Merciful. And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind, until the earth seemed constrained to them despite its vastness and their souls seemed constrained to them} until He reached: {O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with those who are true}. Ka'b said: By Allah, Allah has never bestowed upon me any blessing after He guided me to Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)—that I did not lie to him and perish as those who lied perished. Indeed, Allah said concerning those who lied when He revealed the revelation the worst of what He said to anyone, and Allah said: {They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them that you would leave them alone. So turn away from them; indeed they are impure; and their refuge is Hell as recompense for what they used to earn. They swear to you so that you might be satisfied with them; but even if you should be satisfied with them, indeed Allah is not satisfied with a defiantly disobedient people}. Ka'b said: We, the three, were left behind from the matter of those from whom the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) accepted when they swore to him, taking their pledge and asking forgiveness for them, while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) deferred our matter until Allah decreed concerning it. It is regarding that that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: {And [He also forgave] the three who were left behind}. And what Allah mentioned of our being left behind was not our staying behind from the expedition; rather, it was his setting us apart and deferring our matter apart from those who swore to him and made excuses to him and he accepted from them. And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated it to me: Hujayn ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from 'Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, with the isnad of Yunus from al-Zuhri, exactly the same.
